subject: Banking
title: QR Code Payments in China
description: A 60-second lesson on QR Code Payments in China.

hook.text: In China, street food vendors display QR codes. Customers scan, pay, and walk away. Cash barely exists in daily life.

buildup.text: Alipay and WeChat Pay dominate with over 1.5 billion combined users.

discovery.text: QR payments are cheap. No card terminal needed. A printed piece of paper with a code becomes a payment acceptance.

twist.text: The Chinese government worries about Alipay and WeChat's power. Two companies control most of the nation's payment data.

climax.text: QR payments show that the cheapest infrastructure wins. A printed code beats a $500 card terminal.

punchline.text: A printed QR code replaces card terminals. China went mobile-first.

quiz.question: Why did QR code payments dominate in China over card networks?
options: QR codes need no expensive merchant terminal hardware
